question: Mahmud Begada was a famous sultan of which Sultanate? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Jaunpur
Malwa
Gujarat
Bengal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gujarat

Explanation:
Mahmud Begada was the famous sultan of the Gujarat Sultanate. His real name was Sultan Mahmud Shah I and he belonged to the Muzaffarid dynasty of the Gujarat Sultanate. He ruled from 1458 to 1511 CE. The title 'Begada' was given to him because he captured two major forts. He conquered the forts of Champaner and Junagadh. Mahmud Begada shifted his capital from Ahmedabad to Muhammadabad (present-day Champaner). He was a skilled military commander and administrator. During his reign, the Gujarat Sultanate reached its peak of power. He also fought against the Portuguese. His reign marked significant expansion and consolidation of the sultanate.

☛ Which two forts did Mahmud Begada capture? → Champaner and Junagadh
question_hi: महमूद बेगड़ा किस सल्तनत का प्रसिद्ध सुल्तान था? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: जौनपुर
मालवा
गुजरात
बंगाल

Solution: सही उत्तर है गुजरात

Explanation:
महमूद बेगड़ा गुजरात सल्तनत का प्रसिद्ध सुल्तान था। उसका वास्तविक नाम सुल्तान महमूद शाह प्रथम था और वह गुजरात सल्तनत के मुजफ्फरिद वंश का शासक था। उसने 1458 से 1511 ईस्वी तक शासन किया। 'बेगड़ा' उपनाम उसे दो प्रमुख किलों पर विजय प्राप्त करने के कारण मिला था। उसने चंपानेर और जूनागढ़ के किलों पर कब्जा किया था। महमूद बेगड़ा ने अपनी राजधानी अहमदाबाद से स्थानांतरित कर मुहम्मदाबाद (वर्तमान चंपानेर) बनाई। वह एक कुशल सेनापति और प्रशासक था। उसके शासनकाल में गुजरात सल्तनत अपनी शक्ति के चरम पर थी। उसने पुर्तगालियों से भी संघर्ष किया था।

question: Who established the Chishti sect in India? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Moinuddin Chishti
Khwaja Nizamuddin Auliya
Khwaja Saleem Chishti
Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Moinuddin Chishti

Explanation:
The Chishti sect in India was established by Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti in the 12th century. He settled in Ajmer (Rajasthan), where his shrine (dargah) is located. The Chishti order is a prominent Sufi tradition emphasizing love, service, and music. Moinuddin Chishti is also known as Garib Nawaz (favorer of the poor). His notable successors include Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki, Baba Farid, and Nizamuddin Auliya, who expanded the order across India.

question: Who composed the famous book 'Kitab-ul-Hind'? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Al-Biruni
Rich Khusro
Abdur Razzak
Ibn Arabi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Al-Biruni

Explanation:
The famous book 'Kitab-ul-Hind' was composed by Al-Biruni in the 11th century. This book provides a detailed account of Indian culture, religion, philosophy, science, and social life. Al-Biruni was a Persian scholar who came to India with Mahmud of Ghazni. He deeply studied Sanskrit and wrote this treatise in Arabic. 'Kitab-ul-Hind' is considered an authentic source on Indian history and culture. It covers topics like Indian astronomy, mathematics, medicine, and religious practices. Al-Biruni's objective and analytical approach made this work unique for its time.

question: Who among the following introduced the practice of branding of horses?  (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Babar
Balban
Akbar
Allauddin Khilji
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Allauddin Khilji

Explanation:
Allauddin Khilji (1296-1316) introduced the practice of branding horses. This was part of his administrative and military reforms. The purpose of this practice was to identify royal horses and prevent fraud in the army. A special mark was branded on each horse's body, indicating its ownership and quality. This maintained discipline in the army and ensured availability of horses during wars. This reform was a significant aspect of Allauddin's efficient administrative policies.

question: The word 'Silsila' is related to which of the following? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Sufi Sampraday
Sikh Sampraday
Imperial Decree
Devotional Sect
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sufi Sampraday

Explanation:
The word ‘Silsila’ is related to Sufi Sampraday. It is an Arabic word meaning ‘chain’ or ‘lineage’. In the Sufi tradition, ‘Silsila’ refers to the spiritual lineage through which Sufi teachings and spiritual knowledge are transmitted from a master to a disciple. Each Silsila follows the tradition of a specific Sufi saint, such as the Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiri, and Naqshbandi orders. This concept represents the spiritual continuity and the master-disciple tradition in Sufism. Among the other options, the Sikh tradition has a ‘Guru lineage’, an Imperial Decree is a royal order, and the Devotional Sect (Bhakti) does not have a similar chain.

☛ What are the major Sufi Silsilas? → Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiri, Naqshbandi
☛ From which language is the word Silsila derived? → Arabic
☛ What is the chain of Sufi orders called? → Silsila
☛ Which Sufi Silsila was established first in India? → Chishti Silsila
question_hi: 'सिलसिला' शब्द इनमें से किस से संबंधित है? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 3)

शाही फरमान
भक्ति संप्रदाय
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है सूफी संप्रदाय

Explanation:
‘सिलसिला’ शब्द सूफी संप्रदाय से संबंधित है। यह एक अरबी शब्द है जिसका अर्थ ‘श्रृंखला’ या ‘कड़ी’ होता है। सूफी परंपरा में ‘सिलसिला’ उस आध्यात्मिक वंश को दर्शाता है जिसके माध्यम से सूफी शिक्षाएँ और आध्यात्मिक ज्ञान एक गुरु से शिष्य तक प्रसारित होते हैं। प्रत्येक सिलसिला एक विशिष्ट सूफी संत की परंपरा को मानता है, जैसे कि चिश्ती, सुहरावर्दी, कादिरी और नक्शबंदी। यह अवधारणा सूफीवाद की आध्यात्मिक निरंतरता और गुरु-शिष्य परंपरा को दर्शाती है। अन्य विकल्पों में सिक्ख संप्रदाय में ‘गुरु परंपरा’ है, शाही फरमान शासकीय आदेश है, और भक्ति संप्रदाय में इसी तरह की परंपरा नहीं है।

question: The Bahamani state was the most powerful under whose rule?  (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Alauddin Hassan
Firoz Shah Bahman
Ahmed Shah
Mahmoud Gavan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahmoud Gavan

Explanation:
The Bahamani state was most powerful under the rule of Mahmoud Gavan, a prime minister (Vazir) who effectively controlled the administration. From 1466 to 1481, he implemented administrative reforms, strengthened the military, and expanded the kingdom's territory. He conquered important regions like Goa and Bidar. Under his leadership, the Bahamani Sultanate reached its peak in military power and economic prosperity. He led successful campaigns against the Vijayanagara Empire and neighboring states. Although not a sultan, his policies made the Bahamani state a dominant force in the Deccan. After his execution, the kingdom weakened and eventually fragmented. His period is considered the golden era of the Bahamani Sultanate.

☛ Under which sultan did Mahmoud Gavan serve? → Muhammad Shah III

☛ What was the capital of the Bahamani state under Mahmoud Gavan? → Bidar

question: Which one of the following devotional saints have projected the philosophy of Shuddha advaita? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 1)

Shankaracharya
Madhavacharya
Ramanand
solution:

Explanation:
Shuddha Advaita (pure non-dualism) is a prominent school of Vedanta, propagated by Vallabhacharya (1479-1531). Vallabhacharya founded the Pushti Marg, emphasizing devotion to Lord Krishna. In contrast, Shankaracharya propounded Advaita, Madhavacharya Dvaita, and Ramananda Vishishtadvaita. Hence, Vallabhacharya is the correct exponent of Shuddha Advaita.

question: Mughal miniature painting reached its peak during the rule of _____  (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 1)

question: Who among the following has plundered and destroyed Somnath Temple 17 times along with other temples in his attacks? (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 2)

question: The famous Borobudur Temple is dedicated to _______. (RPF SI(06/01/2019) Shift 2)

Shiva
Buddha
solution:

Explanation:

The temple walls feature 2,672 relief panels depicting the life and teachings of Buddha.

question: Which of the following turned the Sikhs into a military sect? (RPF SI 2018 (06/01/2019) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following Sultans of Delhi is known for its market control policy?  (RPF SI 2018 (10/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Qutbuddin Aibak
Firuz Shah Tughlaq
Muhammad bin Tughluq
Allauddin Khilji
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Allauddin Khilji

Explanation:
Allauddin Khilji (1296-1316) was the Sultan of Delhi known for his economic reforms and market control policy. He implemented a strict administrative system to control prices of essential commodities like food grains, cloth, horses, and other goods. He appointed officials such as 'Diwan-i-Riyasat' and 'Shahna-i-Mandi' to monitor the markets. Allauddin imposed severe punishments for black marketing and hoarding to enforce price controls. His policy aimed to maintain a large army at low salaries and defend against Mongol invasions. Under this policy, all traders had to register, and prices were fixed by the government. This system is considered one of the earliest examples of state-controlled markets in medieval India.
